spec: docs/SPEC.md section 2, 'Clean-build and target isolation proofs'
note: This manifest is closed. A receipt fails on anything it does not list, so
widening MAS is an edit here and nowhere else. It is consumed by
scripts/mas-isolation-receipts.py, which emits the four coupled receipts
the specification requires.
The App Store bundle identifier is deliberately absent: it belongs to
submission, which decision 5 defers, and no receipt needs it.

product.name: allward-mas
product.reason: The sandboxed, remote-only product of decision 5, built from the same revision as the Developer ID product.

forbidden_targets.name: AllwardLocalPTY
forbidden_targets.reason: Local child PTY lifecycle. SPEC section 2 places it absent from the MAS link graph.

forbidden_targets.name: AllwardLocalPublisherEndpoint
forbidden_targets.reason: App-owned AF_UNIX receiver and listener lifecycle. SPEC section 2 places it absent from the MAS link graph.

forbidden_targets.name: CAllwardPTY
forbidden_targets.reason: forkpty shim reached only through AllwardLocalPTY, so it is a target-only dependency the same exclusion covers.

forbidden_capabilities.reason: MAS is remote-only, which is a product rule and not a sandbox limitation. Measured on macOS 26.5.2, App Sandbox PERMITS spawning /usr/bin/ssh; the child inherits the sandbox and then cannot read ~/.ssh/config, known_hosts, or any key, so the spawn buys nothing. See docs/evidence/SANDBOX.md. The capability is forbidden because a product labelled MAS must offer no local shell and no helper that provides one.

A sandboxed product owns no listener path outside its container, and SPEC section 2 excludes the listener module. Connecting an AF_UNIX client socket is not forbidden, so only the listener calls appear here.
source_pattern_note: These match the syscall, not a method that happens to share its name.
A leading Darwin. or Foundation. qualifier counts; any other qualifier
means a call on some object, and a preceding 'func' means a declaration.
Receipt 4's symbol scan is the authority for the raw calls, because an
undefined _bind or _listen in a Mach-O image cannot be anything else.

forbidden_capabilities.reason: The sandbox cannot reach the ssh-agent socket. OQ-14 and decision D-B own the MAS credential route; until then no code may assume an agent.
SPEC section 2 forbids shared code from assuming /tmp. A sandboxed product has a container, not a shared temporary directory.

note: An entry grants one file one capability, and must name the reviewed
construct and why the sandbox permits it. Empty is the correct state:
an exemption is a hole in the proof, not a convenience.
Each fixture MUST fail to compile against the MAS target closure, and the
diagnostic MUST name at least one string in must_not_resolve. Requiring a
name is what stops a typo or an unrelated error from passing as isolation.
A missing module stops compilation at the import, so the module name alone
may be the only one that appears.

entries.reason: Local child PTY lifecycle. MAS is remote-only.
App-owned AF_UNIX receiver and listener lifecycle.
Binds and listens on a socket path from inside shared AllwardChrome.
Runs the herdr argv through a child process from inside shared AllwardChrome.

note: The complete set of Mach-O images the receipts inspect inside a MAS
archive. Anything present in the archive and missing here fails receipt 4,
which is what makes the set closed rather than advisory.
MAS carries no MCP helper executable yet: SPEC section 15 grants MAS the
MCP surface, but the transport that reaches it under sandbox is phase 4
and phase 5 work. Adding the helper is an edit to this list.

executables.reason: The application binary. Its Mach-O closure is the subject of receipts 3 and 4.

note: System dylibs and frameworks the MAS binary is permitted to link.
Receipt 3 fails on any linked library outside this list, which is how a
new dependency arrives as a decision rather than as a surprise.
Paths are matched as prefixes so the OS version-stamped suffixes
otool reports do not have to be frozen here.
Phase 6 archives the product and validates these. Listed here so the
sandbox posture is reviewable before an archive exists.
com.apple.security.app-sandbox is what makes this the MAS product;
network.client is what leaves it able to reach a remote host at all.
